journey.body: The course follows an engineered energy-service chain through six changes of scale. It does not trace one electron or claim that Abilene's grid and onsite sources form one evidenced as-built path. Each phase first explains the generic mechanism, then maps only supported parts onto the Abilene reference campus, and finally exposes the constraint handed onward.

facts.basis: ERCOT's rule record supplies the effective date. Its 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-21 Market Notices document the missed original classification milestone, the PUCT exceptions, and ERCOT's stated conditional-classification intent.
facts.scope: Public Batch Zero process posture through the 2026-08-21 notice; no inference about later notices, final classifications, individual projects, study completion, allocation, agreement, construction, or energization
facts.value: Batch Zero became effective on 2026-07-11, but ERCOT did not issue the classifications contemplated for 2026-08-07 after a required data-center verification step. The PUCT granted ERCOT's requested near-term good-cause exceptions on 2026-08-20, and ERCOT stated on 2026-08-21 that it intended to issue conditional classifications by 2026-08-31. That stated intention is not evidence that conditional or final classifications were issued.

facts.basis: PGRR145 Sections 9.2 through 9.6 establish submission, modeling, study, allocation, agreement, refinement, telemetry, and energization gates. ERCOT's August notices supersede the original near-term classification deadline without changing these coarse engineering categories.
facts.scope: Approved ERCOT Batch Zero process design, subject to the August 2026 timeline exceptions; not a universal large-load process or schedule, an Abilene status claim, an energization approval, a constructed-upgrade claim, or an allowed-MW claim for any project
facts.value: Under the approved transitional Batch Zero procedure, the coarse gates are eligibility and submission of project data, dynamic models, and a preliminary Load Commissioning Plan; a system-wide steady-state and stability-screening study; peak-demand allocation, identified transmission improvements, and an interconnection-agreement commitment; refinement of the needed improvements and a short-circuit study; then, before Initial Energization, satisfaction of ERCOT-established conditions, which may include network-model inclusion, operational and accurate telemetry, required stability or SSO work, and a current Load Commissioning Plan. Applicable PCLR and WLPUN paths also require written ERCOT confirmation and enforce their documented demand or withdrawal limits.

facts.basis: ERCOT's current Large Load Integration page identifies the load-facility threshold and process participants.
facts.scope: ERCOT Batch Zero threshold statement as accessed; eligibility must be checked against PGRR145 and current notices, and this is not an approval for any project
facts.value: ERCOT's current Batch Zero process addresses qualifying load facilities of 75 MW or greater seeking to interconnect to the ERCOT system.

facts.basis: The current FERC pro forma LGIP organizes the process around Sections 3, 7 through 9, 11, and 12. Its facilities study identifies the equipment, upgrades, construction scope, cost, and estimated construction time, and the LGIA governs commencement and construction activities.
facts.scope: FERC pro forma process for generating facilities above 20 MW; not every jurisdiction or transmission-provider tariff, not an ERCOT large-load path, and not a universal project schedule, approval, or outcome
facts.value: In FERC's pro forma process for large generating facilities, the coarse gates are a valid interconnection request with required project data and readiness items; cluster and any affected-system studies; an interconnection facilities study that defines required equipment, interconnection facilities, network upgrades, construction work, cost, and schedule; an executed or unexecuted-filed Large Generator Interconnection Agreement; and performance of the agreed interconnection and upgrade construction activities.

facts.basis: FERC's explainer states that the rule addresses study and connection of generating facilities.
facts.scope: FERC-jurisdictional generator interconnection rule; not an ERCOT large-load process or project schedule
facts.value: FERC Order No. 2023 reforms transmission-provider processes used to study and connect generating facilities, including many storage projects, to the transmission system.

For inference, multiply matching accelerator watts by tokens per joule measured for the exact model, weights or quantization, hardware, software, batching, input/output distribution, quality, and latency boundary; or scale exact-system tokens per second with matching system count and measured scale efficiency. For an energy-yield route, start with facility energy over the interval, derive matching IT energy, then use measured accelerator-energy share and matching tokens per joule, or integrate the rate route over the same interval, to produce token count. facts.basis: Algebra from the ISO PUE definition, with the standard's period and boundary preserved.
facts.scope: Energy-accounting step in a hypothetical scenario; not an Abilene estimate
facts.value: For a matching continuous 12-month boundary, scenario IT energy equals scenario total data-center energy divided by scenario PUE. An average-power route instead requires direct IT-power metering or a boundary-matched interim or partial PUE over the same averaging interval; annual PUE must not be silently treated as a point-in-time operating ratio.

facts.basis: MLCommons defines distinct scenarios, metrics, quality gates, and LLM latency measures.
facts.scope: MLPerf Inference methodology; not an Abilene benchmark result
facts.value: A defensible inference-throughput result names the model, dataset or workload, quality target, scenario, system under test, and latency constraints. MLPerf separates Offline measured throughput from Server maximum supported throughput under benchmark-specific latency limits and records time to first token and time per output token for LLMs.

facts.basis: The recipe preserves ISO energy boundaries, NVIDIA product/runtime distinctions, the PaLM training-MFU definition, and MLPerf measurement constraints without substituting product nameplate for observed operation.
facts.scope: General teaching recipe; produces no Abilene token estimate
facts.value: Choose one output and one common averaging interval. For a power-rate route, start with measured average facility power over that interval; obtain matching average IT power from direct metering or a boundary-matched interim or partial PUE, then obtain accelerator power from direct metering or a measured IT-power share. For training, supply exact active hardware quantity, applicable aggregate peak matmul FLOP/s, and MFU measured for the same model and system; divide aggregate peak FLOP/s times MFU by model FLOPs per token. Apply a separate fleet active-duty factor only when MFU is conditional on active execution, and reconcile the inventory's measured power with accelerator power. For inference, multiply matching accelerator watts by tokens per joule measured for the exact model, weights or quantization, hardware, software, batching, input/output distribution, quality, and latency boundary; or scale exact-system tokens per second with matching system count and measured scale efficiency. For an energy-yield route, start with facility energy over the interval, derive matching IT energy, then use measured accelerator-energy share and matching tokens per joule, or integrate the rate route over the same interval, to produce token count. Annual PUE is valid only for its matching annual boundary. Propagate ranges and stop with no estimate when any required site input is unavailable.

facts.basis: The standard defines the numerator, denominator, period, and IT-equipment boundary.
facts.scope: ISO/IEC 30134-2:2026 PUE; not an Abilene measurement
facts.value: PUE is total data-center energy consumption over a continuous 12-month period divided by IT-equipment energy consumption over the same period; IT equipment includes equipment used to store, process, and transport data.

facts.basis: The PaLM authors define MFU and distinguish it from hardware FLOPs utilization.
facts.scope: Training-system analysis in the PaLM paper; not inference utilization or Abilene MFU
facts.value: Model FLOPs utilization is observed training throughput in tokens per second divided by the theoretical maximum token throughput of the same system operating at peak FLOPs, counting the model-required forward and backward operations rather than implementation-dependent rematerialization.

facts.scope: Generic rack-manifold-distributed Technology Cooling System loop; no temperature, flow, coolant, pressure, or site topology is asserted.

synthesis.body: The engineered service chain can now be inspected through three system-level questions without pretending that every branch is one traced physical path or inventing an additional physical phase.

phase_readings.phase_1_generation: Ask whether the selected source has crossed permit, installation, commissioning, and measured-output gates at an electrical interface.
phase_readings.phase_2_transmission: Ask whether interconnection, voltage transformation, transfer equipment, and energized grid service establish deliverable power rather than a nameplate total.
phase_readings.phase_3_campus: Ask whether independent source and feeder branches, protective interruption, and isolation conditions actually preserve service after a disturbance.
phase_readings.phase_4_building: Ask whether building equipment and A/B paths can deliver facility AC to the particular rack, including compatible load interfaces and maintenance isolation.
phase_readings.phase_5_compute: Ask whether rack and board conversion, installed accelerators, workload activity, and measured operating demand turn facility power into useful work.
phase_readings.phase_6_heat: Ask whether component, liquid, residual-air, facility-loop, and atmospheric-rejection boundaries can remove heat under actual operating conditions.

lenses.question: Which evidenced physical, interconnection, construction, equipment, or operating gate currently limits the usable path?
lenses.title: Where does delivery actually bind?

phase_readings.phase_1_generation: Separate generator owner and operator, fuel supply, storage, standby, and contractual-attribute roles before assigning physical delivery.
phase_readings.phase_2_transmission: Separate generator, transmission owner and operator, grid operator, interconnection customer, and site roles at each electrical boundary.
phase_readings.phase_3_campus: Separate utility service, campus sources, campus distribution, building feeder, and protective-device ownership; keep the source merge unknown where evidence is absent.
phase_readings.phase_4_building: Separate campus-feeder, building power-train, maintenance, and IT load-interface responsibility.
phase_readings.phase_5_compute: Separate facilities power, rack hardware, platform operation, and workload ownership before assigning output or utilization risk.
phase_readings.phase_6_heat: Separate IT cooling loop, facility loop, air-side cooling, heat-rejection plant, and water-account responsibility.

lenses.question: Who builds, owns, finances, operates, and bears utilization risk at each boundary?
lenses.title: Who owns the handoff and its risk?

phase_readings.phase_1_generation: Generation MW is only a source-side rating; it is not delivered IT power, accelerators, workload activity, or useful output.
phase_readings.phase_2_transmission: Grid ratings and interconnection capacity are not current site demand or rack power.
phase_readings.phase_3_campus: Campus service and feeder capability are not the count of energized buildings, racks, accelerators, or live workloads.
phase_readings.phase_4_building: Power at a rack position is not board input, processor-rail power, active silicon, or useful workload output.
phase_readings.phase_5_compute: An estimate requires measured electrical inputs, installed hardware, workload configuration, and observed throughput or utilization on the same basis.
phase_readings.phase_6_heat: Cooling capacity and design posture constrain availability but do not quantify useful compute; use measured operating power, thermal state, and output.
